name: Bhabhi
description: Bhabhi (meaning 'Brother's Wife' in Hindi/Punjabi, here implying a teasing burden) is a very popular shedding game in South Asia, particularly in India and Pakistan. Known as 'Getaway' in the West, it is a game of 'active avoidance' where players race to get rid of all their cards. The last player holding cards is christened the 'Bhabhi'—the loser. The game is defined by its brutal 'Thulla' mechanic: if a player cannot follow suit, the player who currently played the highest card of the led suit must pick up the entire pile.

overview.description: Bhabhi (meaning 'Brother's Wife' in Hindi/Punjabi, here implying a teasing burden) is a very popular shedding game in South Asia, particularly in India and Pakistan. Known as 'Getaway' in the West, it is a game of 'active avoidance' where players race to get rid of all their cards. The last player holding cards is christened the 'Bhabhi'—the loser. The game is defined by its brutal 'Thulla' mechanic: if a player cannot follow suit, the player who currently played the highest card of the led suit must pick up the entire pile.

history.origins: Originated in the Punjab region of South Asia. While it shares some DNA with European shedding games, its unique 'highest-card-penalty' rules are distinctly South Asian.
timeline: Mid-20th Century: Bhabhi becomes a standard social game in South Asian households.
1990s: Gains international visibility as 'Getaway' via the global South Asian diaspora.
Present: A staple of digital card gaming in India and Pakistan.
history.cultural: Typically played with high-energy verbal teasing. The term 'Bhabhi' is used lightheartedly but signifies the 'burden' of the losing cards.
history.evolution: The game focuses purely on avoidance (not being the last player) rather than winning, a psychological shift from traditional card games.

setup.players: 3 to 6 players; 4 players provides the best balance of suit distribution.
setup.dealing: Deal the entire deck clockwise as equally as possible. Some players may have one extra card depending on the player count.

rules.objective: Get rid of all cards in your hand. Avoid being the last player remaining with cards.
rules.gameplay: 1. **Start**: The player holding the Ace of Spades leads it. 2. **Trick**: Each player must follow suit if possible. 3. **The Thulla (Break)**: If a player cannot follow suit, they play a card from another suit (a 'Thulla'). This ends the trick immediately. 4. **Penalty**: The player who played the HIGHEST card of the led suit must pick up the entire pile (including the Thulla). 5. **Lead**: The penalized player leads the next trick. 6. **Escape**: Players who empty their hand successfully 'get away' and are safe.
keyRules: Must follow suit if you hold a card of that suit.
The 'Highest Card' is always the highest of the suit originally LED.
If everyone follows suit, the highest card winner simply leads next (no penalty).

strategy.basic: Get rid of your highest cards (Aces, Kings) when you are certain everyone else can follow suit.
strategy.intermediate: Duck the Highs: If you suspect a 'Thulla' is coming (e.g., someone is low on a suit), play a low card of that suit even if you have a high one to avoid being the highest player.
strategy.advanced: Void Management: Purposely create a void in a suit so you can throw your high cards from other suits onto opponents when they lead that suit.
tips: The goal is not to win tricks, but to lose your cards.
Save a 2 or 3 of each suit as 'insurance' to play when you are afraid of a pickup penalty.

variations.name: Bhabhi Thulla
variations.description: A variant where being caught with the final cards results in specific household penalties (e.g., performing a task).
variations.emptyOverridesReason: This variant only changes social or household penalties and does not alter engine rules or parameters.

scoring.description: No formal point system is used. Each deal produces a single loser—the last player holding cards—though groups may optionally track how many times each player loses over a session.
scoring.winCondition: Successful shedding of all cards in hand.

synthesis.shortDescription: The ultimate game of survival. Shed your cards, duck the penalties, and do whatever it takes to avoid becoming the Bhabhi. A ruthless shedding game where one mistake can leave you holding the entire deck.
